---
title: "About"
description: "Who wrote the course, how it is licensed, how to cite it, and how to contribute."
---

*Snakemake for genomics* is a two-day course on writing data pipelines with
Snakemake, built around real public ChIP-seq and DNase-seq data and the lab's
own pipelines. It is written by **JP Flores**.

The course follows the format of the
[HBC training modules](https://hbctraining.github.io/main/): a page per
topic with learning objectives and time estimates, exercises with public
answer keys, and an open license. Each lesson is one
[Quarto](https://quarto.org) file that renders both as a web page and as
reveal.js slides.

| Code: RegPipe, the stopping points, scripts, the site's extensions | [MIT](https://opensource.org/license/mit) | [`LICENSE-code`](LICENSE-code) |
| Lab pipelines in `pipelines/` | their own licenses, in each repository | |
| Course data in `data/` | public ENCODE, UCSC and GEO data under their own terms | [`data/README.md`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/snakemake-course/blob/main/data/README.md) |

Under CC BY 4.0 you may copy, adapt and teach from these lessons, including
in paid courses, as long as you credit the original and link to the license.
A line such as this is enough:

> Adapted from *Snakemake for genomics* by JP Flores,
> <https://jpflores-13.github.io/snakemake-course>, CC BY 4.0.

## How to cite {#how-to-cite}

The repository has a [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff) file, so GitHub shows a
*Cite this repository* button with APA and BibTeX. In text:

> Flores JP. *Snakemake for genomics: a hands-on course* (version 0.1.0).
> <https://github.com/jpflores-13/snakemake-course>

If you use Snakemake in your own work, also cite the Snakemake paper (see
[References](references.qmd)).

## Contributing

Corrections and improvements are welcome, from a typo to a new exercise.

- **Found a mistake or something unclear?** Open an
  [issue](https://github.com/jpflores-13/snakemake-course/issues), or use
  *Report an issue* at the right of any page.
- **Want to fix it yourself?** Use *Edit this page*, or fork the repository
  and open a pull request. The [README](https://github.com/jpflores-13/snakemake-course#readme)
  explains how to build the site locally with `quarto preview`.
- **Teaching the course?** We would like to hear how it went: which modules ran
  long, which exercises confused people.

A few conventions keep the lessons consistent:

- Real pipeline code is never pasted into a page. Pages pull it from the
  pipelines with the `snippet` shortcode, so it cannot drift from the code.
- Command output on the pages (dry runs, DAGs) comes from real runs made when
  the site is built, not typed by hand.
- Every exercise links to an answer that explains *why*.
- Plain language, second person, short sentences.

## Acknowledgments

The course data come from the [ENCODE](https://www.encodeproject.org/)
project, the [UCSC Genome Browser](https://genome.ucsc.edu/) and
[GEO](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/). Snakemake is developed by Johannes
Köster and many contributors.
